CONTEXT: Brandon says the slow test suite cripples the game rework. A quiet full run is about 2 minutes on 16 cores and 1,172 CPU seconds; 12 files hold about 900 of those seconds (tests/test_game_path_journeys.py 411 s, test_evidence_gap_journeys 100, test_bench_item_facts 73, test_3c_no_close_arm 52, test_narration_corpus 47, test_markdown_story_package 42, test_persona_escalation 37, test_scene_2a_advantages 28, test_three_c_prefix 27, test_3c_carried_start 24, test_canon_journey 19, test_late_scene_repro 18). Read docs/testing-runbook.md, docs/agent-workflow-guide.md, tests/shard_durations.json (schema: version, files -> seconds per test file) and tests/conftest.py. Decision (Brandon, 2026-10-24): Ringer worker attempts and checks use a QUICK TIER, and the full suite runs only in CI and before merge.

GOAL: (1) Create scripts/quick_suite.py: runs pytest with `-q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider -n auto` on the whole tests/ tree EXCEPT the heavy files, where heavy files are derived from tests/shard_durations.json (every file whose recorded seconds are at least --threshold, default 15) so the list never goes stale; `--also PATH...` re-includes named heavy files (or any test path) so a task that changes one area still runs its journeys; `--list` prints the selected and skipped files with seconds and the predicted quick-tier CPU seconds and exits; unknown arguments after `--` go to pytest; it prints at the end which heavy files were skipped and the exact command to run them, and exits with pytest's status. It must use `sys.executable`, set TMPDIR=/tmp if unset, work from the repository root regardless of cwd, and never pipe pytest through anything that masks its exit status. (2) Hermetic tests in tests/test_quick_suite.py for the selection logic with a fake durations file (threshold edges, --also re-inclusion, files missing from the durations file are included, skipped list reporting), without running pytest recursively. (3) Docs, kept short: in docs/testing-runbook.md section 1 add at most 4 lines naming `uv run python scripts/quick_suite.py [--also ...]` (what it skips, that CI and merges still run everything); in docs/agent-workflow-guide.md state the Ringer check convention: a manifest check runs scripts/quick_suite.py (with --also for the journeys or heavy files relevant to the change) plus ruff, and the full suite runs in CI and before merge; also say a worker's own verification should use the quick tier and run the full suite at most once, at the end. Read the guides' existing style and edit in place; do not add result logs. (4) Measure and report: wall and CPU for the quick tier vs the full suite on this machine, run each twice, with the load average at the start.

OWNED FILES: scripts/quick_suite.py, tests/test_quick_suite.py, docs/testing-runbook.md, docs/agent-workflow-guide.md. Nothing else.

HOW TO RUN: first confirm PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)" prints a path inside the cwd. Focused: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov -n auto <files> --durations=15. FULL suite must end green: same with no file args. Ruff on Python files you touch: -m ruff check --fix then -m ruff format. Do not run uv. Tests stay hermetic. Do NOT git commit, do NOT git add -A, do NOT touch .git. Measure timings on whatever load the machine has and say so; do not claim a speed-up you did not measure twice.

NOTES CONTRACT: quicktier-notes.md with sections: SCRIPT (flags, selection rule), TESTS, DOCS CHANGED (file and the added lines), MEASUREMENTS (quick tier vs full: wall, CPU, load average, both runs), OPEN QUESTIONS (or 'none'). Reply with a short summary.
tasks.check: bash -c 'set -uo pipefail; N=/home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/game-reimagination-phase1-notes/quicktier-notes.md; [ -s $N ] || { echo FAIL no notes; exit 1; }; PY=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python; git add -A -- scripts/quick_suite.py tests/test_quick_suite.py docs/testing-runbook.md docs/agent-workflow-guide.md; bad=$(git status --porcelain | grep -v -E "^[AMD]  (scripts/quick_suite.py|tests/test_quick_suite.py|docs/testing-runbook.md|docs/agent-workflow-guide.md)$" || true); [ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "FAIL stray files:"; echo "$bad"; exit 1; }; [ -f tests/test_quick_suite.py ] || { echo FAIL no loader test; exit 1; }; OUT=/home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/game-reimagination-phase1-patches; mkdir -p $OUT; git diff --cached > $OUT/quicktier.patch; [ -s $OUT/quicktier.patch ] || { echo FAIL empty patch; exit 1; }; if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -q "^storygame/"; then echo FAIL storygame edited; exit 1; fi; PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp $PY -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov -n auto 2>&1 | tail -25; [ ${PIPESTATUS[0]} -eq 0 ] || { echo FAIL full suite; exit 1; }; $PY -m ruff check storygame tests scripts/quick_suite.py && $PY -m ruff format --check storygame tests scripts/quick_suite.py || exit 1; echo PASS'
tasks.verified: Quick-tier script with tests and short docs; full suite and ruff green

You are a test-infrastructure worker editing the freytag-forge repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge, detached at HEAD. Write short notes to /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/game-reimagination-phase1-notes/journeys-notes.md.

CONTEXT: Brandon says the slow test suite cripples the game rework, and approved restructuring the whole-game journey tests. tests/test_game_path_journeys.py takes about 411 CPU seconds (about 60 journeys of about 9 s each) and tests/test_evidence_gap_journeys.py about 100. Each journey is a deterministic scripted walk of the whole game from turn 0 (see `play(preferred)` in test_game_path_journeys.py): it follows the default thorough policy and deviates only on the first turn where a preferred realization is offered (and with sibling realizations `blocked` from the projection). So the walk before that first deviation is identical to the default walk. Read both journey files, storygame/personas.py (_ScriptedProvider, _select_thorough), storygame/runtime/state.py (snapshot, restore_snapshot) and docs/testing-runbook.md. A previous attempt to speed up the engine's fact lookups gave only about 11 percent, so do not touch storygame/**.

RULE: keep every assertion and every test name; the journeys must give exactly the same results as today. Only change how the shared prefix is computed.

GOAL: (1) Build a helper tests/journey_prefix.py that walks the default policy once per xdist worker (cached) and records, before each turn, a restorable snapshot (RuntimeSnapshot) plus the Journey accumulators so far (picked, forced_exits, scenes, entry_texts) and the provider state needed to continue. For a journey with its own `preferred` and `blocked` sets, replay the decision function at each recorded default state (restore, project offered candidates, apply this journey's blocked/preferred rule, compare with the default selection) WITHOUT calling engine.turn(); at the first state where the decision differs, restore that snapshot and continue with the normal per-turn loop for the rest of the game. If no deviation occurs, the journey equals the default walk. Preserve the `recovery`-journey special handling (blocked outcomes) exactly. (2) Rewrite `play()` in tests/test_game_path_journeys.py to use the helper, keeping its signature, Journey fields and all test functions and assertions. Do the same for tests/test_evidence_gap_journeys.py only if its walks have the same shape (default policy plus a forced deviation); otherwise leave it and say why. (3) PROVE EQUIVALENCE, once, offline: write a throwaway script in /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/game-reimagination-phase1-notes/ that runs EVERY journey both the old full-walk way (from git HEAD's `play`) and the new way and compares picked, scenes, forced_exits, entry_texts, deadline events, final turn_index, final sorted asserted facts and every turn record; it must report identical for all journeys. Record the output in the notes. (4) Add ONE permanent test, tests/test_journey_prefix_equivalence.py, that replays one early-branch and one late-branch journey with the old full-walk code path (copy the old play loop into the test as `full_walk`) and asserts equality with the shared-prefix result, so snapshot drift is caught; keep it cheap. (5) Measure the CPU and wall of the two journey files before and after, run each twice, say what the load average was, and report honestly if the gain is small. Expect roughly 2x because branch points are spread across the game.

OWNED FILES: tests/journey_prefix.py, tests/test_game_path_journeys.py, tests/test_evidence_gap_journeys.py (only if the shape fits), tests/test_journey_prefix_equivalence.py. Nothing else (no storygame/**, no data/**).

HOW TO RUN: first confirm PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)" prints a path inside the cwd. Focused: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov -n auto <files> --durations=15. FULL suite must end green: same with no file args. Ruff on Python files you touch: -m ruff check --fix then -m ruff format. Do not run uv. Tests stay hermetic. Do NOT git commit, do NOT git add -A, do NOT touch .git. Measure timings on whatever load the machine has and say so; do not claim a speed-up you did not measure twice.

NOTES CONTRACT: journeys-notes.md with sections: DESIGN (what is snapshotted, how the deviation point is found), EQUIVALENCE (the all-journeys comparison result), TIMING (before/after CPU and wall, two runs each, load average), EVIDENCE-GAP FILE (changed or not, why), OPEN QUESTIONS (or 'none'). Reply with a short summary.
